sections.html:
El Mirage is a compact Maricopa County city of 9.95 square miles in the northwest Valley, beside the Agua Fria River and U.S. Route 60 (Grand Avenue). It has 35,820 residents as of July 1, 2025, and downtown Phoenix is about 19 miles southeast on US 60. Youngtown borders it on the east, Glendale on the south and Surprise to the northwest, with unincorporated Sun City to the northeast.

Housing figures show who buys here. Median value of an owner-occupied home is $321,900, owners occupy 69.7% of homes, and owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,533 a month. Median gross rent is $1,806 and median household income is $78,050. With 3.24 people per household, families looking for extra bedrooms and a yard are frequent buyers. The mean trip to work takes 30.1 minutes, so many people commute across the Valley.

Because the city is small, buyers often find a house by its cross streets and the school it feeds. Use both when you describe yours, and give the nearest major road so commuters see the drive at a glance.

An El Mirage owner has three roads. An agent listing exposes the house to the most buyers, but it hangs on showings, the buyer's loan and an appraisal. A sale by owner keeps the commission in your pocket and puts contracts and disclosure forms on your desk. A cash buyer takes the house exactly as it is and may close quickly, with an offer that prices in the repairs and risk.

Let the house and the calendar choose. A tidy, updated home and plenty of time points to a listing. Old repairs, a tenant, an inherited title or a hard deadline point to a direct sale. Whatever you pick, get offers in writing and compare the money you would actually keep.

sections.h2: Luke Air Force Base and aircraft noise
sections.html:
Luke Air Force Base, described as the largest fighter pilot training base in NATO, is close to El Mirage. Jets overhead are a normal subject for houses nearby, so expect a buyer to ask about the noise.

Arizona gives governments a way to put this on record. A.R.S. 28-8485 lets the state, or a political subdivision that operates an airport, designate an airport influence area, defined as property exposed to aircraft noise and overflight. The designating body files a record with the county recorder, which warns owners and would-be purchasers. Find out from your title company or the Maricopa County Recorder whether your parcel lies in a recorded area. Then tell the buyer the answer before the question comes up.

El Mirage requires a permit for new construction, some repairs and alterations, and the remodeling, renovation or enlargement of a building. Building safety and permitting sit in the Development Services department. Since January 2, 2024 the Permit Center has taken all plans online through the ELM Online Permitting portal, and the same department schedules building inspections.

If an earlier owner finished a garage, patio or room addition, request its permit and inspection record from Development Services before you take an offer. Buyers who dream of an addition may also read the General Plan and the zoning ordinance update that Planning and Zoning maintains.

If the house has been rented, the Maricopa County Assessor shows the parcel type as Residential/Rental once a registration is on file. Ask Development Services whether a rental license or short-term rental registration applies to your address.

The Dysart Unified School District serves El Mirage and enrolls roughly 5,500 preK through 12th grade students who live in the city. Elementary schools include El Mirage Elementary, Surprise Elementary, Thompson Ranch Elementary and Riverview Elementary. Dysart Middle School opened in 2021, and the high school choices are Dysart High School, opened in 1963, and Sundown Mountain, an alternative school for 11th and 12th grades. Some residents north of Waddell and Thunderbird Roads are zoned for Valley Vista High School, which sits outside the city.

The zone for your street may differ from a neighbor's. Use the district's boundary lookup for your exact address before you write the listing.

Maricopa County bills El Mirage owners twice a year.

InstallmentDueDelinquent after
First halfOctober 1November 1, after 5 p.m.
Second halfMarch 1May 1, after 5 p.m.

When the first of November lands on a weekend, the deadline moves to the next business day. A bill over $100 can be paid in full through December 31 without interest. Phone the county treasurer for your parcel's balance before closing, so nothing unpaid turns up at the title company.

A sale of an El Mirage house goes on record at the Maricopa County Recorder, for $30 on most documents. Staff there will not take a deed unless it shows an affidavit of property value or an exemption code, and they will not tell you which code is yours. Walk the paperwork into 301 W Jefferson St, Suite 200, Phoenix, or mail it and wait two to four weeks for the originals to return.

The affidavit comes from A.R.S. 11-1133 and asks for the price, sale date, legal description and parcel details. Exemptions live in A.R.S. 11-1134. They cover a deed of gift, a quitclaim given for no money, a conveyance ordered by a court, and a nominal-consideration transfer between spouses, siblings, parents and children, or grandparents and grandchildren. When a family settles a house after a death, one of these often applies. A title officer or attorney can say which.

A cash purchase drops three hurdles that slow a financed deal: the buyer's loan approval, the lender's appraisal, and the repair list a loan can require. Escrow and title still happen, so liens, taxes and the deed move through the same hands. The difference is how long it takes and how many outside parties can stall it.

Before you talk to any buyer, collect your parcel number, newest tax bill, any mortgage payoff figure, and permit records for the garage, patio or additions. Mention aircraft noise, an open permit or a tenant at the outset. A problem found late usually costs you more than one disclosed early.

After you accept, plan your move-out date with the buyer and confirm in writing whether furniture or leftover items may stay. Keep copies of everything you sign, and save the closing statement for your tax records.

faqs.q: How many people live in El Mirage?
faqs.a: The population is 35,820 as of July 1, 2025, nearly the same as the 35,805 counted in 2020. The city covers 9.95 square miles.

faqs.q: Which school district serves El Mirage?
faqs.a: The Dysart Unified School District serves the city, and its schools include El Mirage Elementary, Thompson Ranch Elementary, Riverview Elementary and Dysart High School. Some residents north of Waddell and Thunderbird Roads are zoned for Valley Vista High School.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: The Maricopa County Recorder charges $30 per document for deeds and most other filings. A deed also needs an affidavit of property value or an exemption code before it is accepted.

faqs.q: Is El Mirage close to Luke Air Force Base?
faqs.a: Yes, and aircraft noise is a normal question from buyers. Ask your title company whether an airport influence area is recorded against your parcel.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair a house in El Mirage?
faqs.a: A permit is needed for new construction, some repair work, alterations, remodeling, renovation or enlargement. Plans go in online through the city's permit portal, and Development Services can tell you whether a specific job is covered.
